look_here_first: Start with the flower architecture: a large, open, radial four-petaled primrose—usually pink to white—with 8 stamens and a conspicuous 4-lobed cross/finger-like stigma on a spreading rhizomatous plant.
project_tracker_diagnostic: rhizomatous spreading perennial (sometimes annual); young shoots rosetted; later stems decumbent to ascending; large radial flowers about 25–52 mm across; 4 broad fan- to heart-shaped pink/white petals; 8 stamens and 4-lobed stigma; club-shaped many-seeded 4-valved capsule

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County lists Oenothera speciosa among plants occurring naturally and not introduced. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes multiple Oenothera speciosa specimens. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Oenothera speciosa.

best_field_traits: young shoots rosetted; later stems decumbent to ascending
large radial flowers about 25–52 mm across
4 broad fan- to heart-shaped pink/white petals

comparisons.key_distinctions: Oenothera triloba: Both can have large primrose flowers, but O. triloba is a flat, essentially stemless rosette with yellow flowers borne on an extremely long square floral tube; O. speciosa has leafy stems and a much shorter tube. Oenothera lindheimeri: O. speciosa has a broad radial flower with four spreading petals; O. lindheimeri has the airy 'gaura' look with petals held mainly to the upper side and long projecting stamens.
